t: Japan and China conclude the Agreement concerning Mines and Railways in Manchuria, and Agreement relating to Chientao Region. (Sept. 4). (By the former agreement it was decided that China should previously arrange with Japan in the event of her undertaking to contract a railway between Hsinmintun and Fakumen, that China should recognize the Tashichiao-Yingkow line as a branch line of the S.M.R., that China should recognize the right of Japan to work coal mines of Fushun and Yentai, that all mines along the Antung-Mukden Railway and the main line of the S.M.R., excepting those at Fushun and Yentai, should be exploited as joint enterprises of the Japanese and Chinese, and that Japan should agree to the extension of the Peking-Mukden Railway to the city wall of Mukden. And by the latter agreement the long disputed boundaries between China and Korea was fixed along the Tumen River, and Koreans were given the right to settle freely and own land in the Chientao district.)

(By this Treaty the term of lease of Port Arthur and Dalny and the terms of the S.M.R. and Antung-Mukden Railway were extended to 99 years, namely, the definite time for the expiration of the terms of lease became 1997 for the Kwantung Leased Territory, 2002 for the S.M.R. and 2007 for the Antung-Mukden Railway. Secondly, the Japanese acquired right to lease land by negotiation in South Manchuria. Thirdly, the Japanese acquired rights to reside and travel freely in South Manchuria and to engage in business and manufacture of any kind, and fourthly the Chinese government agreed to give permission to Japanese and Chinese who desire to undertake agricultural enterprises jointly).

a: Appendix — Appendix I. Table of Outstanding Events in or Relating to Manchurian History
t: Nine Power Treaty regarding to Principles and Policies to be followed in matters concerning China signed (Feb. 6). Principle of 'Open Door' affirmed formally by the treaty, and the Powers other than China agree: (1) To respect the sovereignty, the independence, and the territorial and administrative integrity in China; (2) To provide the fullest and unembarrassed opportunity to China to develop and maintain for herself an effective and stable government; (3) To use their influence for the purpose of effectually establishing and maintaining the principle of equal opportunity; and (4) To refrain from taking advantage of conditions in China in order to seek special rights or privileges.

a: Appendix — Appendix I. Table of Outstanding Events in or Relating to Manchurian History
t: Agreement between the Government of the Autonomous Three Eastern Provinces of the Republic of China and the Government of the U.S.S.R., concerning Mutual Rights and Principles signed at Mukden (Sept. 20). The main features of this Agreement are as follows: (1) The Soviet Union recognizes that the C.E.R. is a purely commercial enterprise, (2) In the management of the Railway, the two countries are equally represented, (3) After the expiration of sixty years from August 27, 1896, instead of eighty years, as formerly provided, the railway shall pass by reversion without payment into Chinese possession. China may recover the railway at any time upon paying, with her own capital, the price agreed upon by the two governments. (4) Both parties agree that the future of the C.E.R. shall be determined by the U.S.S.R. and China to the exclusion of any third party or parties. (5) The two governments recognize equal rights of navigation on border rivers, and maintenance of the present border line, and also agree not to engage in propaganda directed against the political and social systems of the other contracting party.

a: Appendix — Appendix I. Table of Outstanding Events in or Relating to Manchurian History
t: War between Yen Hsi-shan and Chiang Kai-shek (Feb.-Sept.).

a: Appendix — Appendix I. Table of Outstanding Events in or Relating to Manchurian History
t: Sino-Japanese Customs Tariff Agreement signed (May 6).

a: Appendix — Appendix I. Table of Outstanding Events in or Relating to Manchurian History
t: Chang Hsueh-liang intervenes between the Northern Army under Yen Hsi-shan and Feng Yu-hsiang, and National Government (Sept. 18). The Mukden troops enter Peking (Sept. 21).

a: Appendix — Appendix I. Table of Outstanding Events in or Relating to Manchurian History
t: Sino-Soviet conference on the C.E.R. matters opened in Moscow (Oct.) (conference continued sporadically; however, up to the end of 1932 no definite agreement reached).
Silver price falls to 13, 11/16 at London market.
Chinese Chamber of Commerce at Harbin proposed to the North-Eastern Political Committee to issue 20,000,000 yuan of Hsien Tayang-piao for relieving the depression in Kirin and Heilungkiang Provinces.
Director Kimura of the S.M.R. Co. discusses railway problems with Chang Hsueh-liang (張學良) at Mukden.
Through traffic arrangement made for three Chinese Railways in Manchuria, viz.: Peiping-Mukden, Mukden-Hailung and Kirin-Hailung railways.
North-Eastern Financial Conference opened.
Communist Army under Chu Te (朱德) threatens Nanchang (南昌).
Chang Tso-hsiang (張作相) visits Director Kimura at Mukden.
Owing to the unfavourable business condition, the C.E.R. dismisses 2,000 employees and cuts salaries by 10 percent.
North-Eastern Telephone, Telegraph and Radio Administration (東北電信管理處) established.
Mo Te-hui (莫德惠) reports on the Sino-Soviet C.E.R. conference to Wang Cheng-ting (王正廷), Nanking Foreign Minister.
Silver price falls to 12, 13/16 at London market.
Serious fall in quotation of Heilungkiang Kuantieh causes the bankruptcy of many merchants.
Liaoning People's Foreign Policy Association (遼寧國民外交協會) demands to have the object of Chang-Kimura negotiation on railway made public.
North-Eastern Financial Conference closed.

Chang Ching-hui (張景惠), Governor of Tungsheng Special District, demands Chang Hsueh-liang to take measures to relieve North Manchurian farmers of the effect of the serious fall of the price of their agricultural products.
Chitung (啟東) Tobacco Co. established at Mukden.
Second conference between Chang Hsueh-liang and Director Kimura takes place at Mukden.
Tangshan (湯山) Conference on Constitution ends in secession of Hu Han-min (胡漢民) from Chiang Kai-shek's (蔣介石) group.
Hu Han-min's resignation accepted by the Standing Committee of the Central Executive Committee of Kuomintang.
Director Kimura meets Kao Chi-yi (高紀毅), Chairman of the North-Eastern Communications Committee.
First formal Sino-Japanese Conference on extraterritoriality; (Conference held several times up to the end of April when the negotiation dropped).
Mo Te-hui leaves Harbin for Moscow.
Provincial Branch of Kuomintang established at Mukden.
Cheng Chi-tang (陳濟棠) and other generals in Canton and Kwanhsi protest to the Nanking Government on the arrest of Hu Han-min.
Huatung Hsinpao (華東新報), organ of the Wang Ching-wei (汪精衛) faction, suppressed by the Nanking authorities.
Negotiation between Great Britain and the Nanking Government on extraterritoriality discontinued.
Mo Te-hui meets Karakhan. Resumption of the Soviet-Chinese Conference agreed.
Strike of Chinese workers in tussah silk filatures at Antung.
Hamaguchi Cabinet of Japan resigns.
Wakatsuki Cabinet formed in Japan.
Chang Hsueh-liang leaves Mukden for Peiping.
Chahar Special District renamed Shuoning (朔寧) Province.
Chen Ming-chu (陳銘樞), Chen Chi-tang, Li Tsung-jen (李宗仁), Pai Chung-hsi (白崇禧), Ku Ying-fen (古應芬) and others issue a circular telegram impeaching Chiang Kai-shek. Canton's dissension movement starts.
Chang Hsueh-liang arrives at Nanking to attend the National People's Convention.
National People's Convention (國民會議).
New export tariff announced by the Nanking Government.
Provisional Constitution of the Republic of China adopted by the National People's Convention.
Chang Chin-hui sworn in as the Chairman of the military Advisory Council of the National Government.
Sun Fo（孫科） leaves Shanghai for Hongkong.
Chen Yu-jen or Eugene Chen（陳友仁） and Sun Fo meet Wang Ching-wei, Tang Shao-yi （唐紹儀）, and other leaders of Canton Secessionists at Hongkong.
Circular telegram demanding the retirement of Chiang Kai-shek issued, Tang Shao-yi being the leading signatory.
Central Executive Committee of Kuomintang formed at Canton.
National Government of Canton established.
Emergency meeting of the Central Executive Committee held at Nanking.
Nanking Government cuts salaries of government officials by 40 percent.
U.S. Senator Pittman arrives at Shanghai.
National Economic Council Act promulgated.
Chinese authorities decline to recognize newly appointed Consul-General Ohashi of Japan at Harbin.
Wu Chao-Shu（伍朝樞）, Chinese Minister at Washington resigns.
President Sengoku of the S.M.R. Co. resigns and Count Uchida appointed as his successor.
Military Conference held at Canton. Military expedition against Nanking discussed.
First meeting of the Fifth Plenary Session of the Central Executive Committee （中央執監全體會議）.
Governor-General Saito of Korea resigns and General Ugaki appointed as his successor.
Official Statement issued by British Consul-General on the Thorburn case.
Chiang Kai-shek leaves Nanking for Kianghsi to supervise the anti-Communist campaign.
Captain Nakamura of the Japanese General Staff murdered between Taonan and Solun.
Quotation of Fengtien-piao falls to 110 yuan for 1 yuan of Hsien Tayang.
Clash between Korean and Chinese farmers at Wanpaoshan (萬寶山).
Anti-Chinese riots occur in various cities of Korea.
Chinese organizations in Harbin resolve anti-Japanese boycott.
Anti-Japanese boycott opened at Shanghai.
Report of the death of Captain Nakamura received by Japanese Consul-General at Tsitsihar.
Anti-Japanese boycott resolved at Hankow.
Clash between the troops of Chang Hsueh-liang and Shi Yu-san's (石友三) Shanhsi (山西) forces.
Shi Yu-san issues a circular telegram denouncing Chiang Kai-shek and pledging support to Canton.
Canton government issues order to start 'punitive expedition' against Nanking.
Negotiations on Wanpaoshan affair opened.
Chang Hsueh-liang announces a punitive expedition against Shi Yu-san.
Eugene Chen, Foreign Minister of the Canton government, arrives at Yokohama.
Anti-Japanese boycott started at Mukden.
Eugene Chen meets Baron Shidehara, Foreign Minister of Japan.
Sino-French agreement on the rendition of the French settlement at Shanghai signed.
Martial law declared in Shanghai, Nanking, Hankow and other cities because of civil war.
Nanking Government protests to Japan on the admission of Eugene Chen to that country.
Shi Yu-san's Shanhsi troops captured at Shichiachwang (石家莊).
Anti-Japanese boycott suppressed by Mukden authorities.
Second interview of Eugene Chen with Baron Shidehara.
Chinese representative at Tokyo requests Japanese authorities to arrest Eugene Chen.
Vanguard of the Kwanghsi troops enter Hunan.
Yen Hsi-shan (閻錫山) flies back to Tatung (大同) from Dairen.
Shigemitsu promoted to the post of Minister of Japan to China.
Report on anti-Chinese riots in Korea submitted to the Nanking Foreign Office by the Chinese Minister at Tokyo.
Yen Shi-shan arrives at Taiyuan (太原).
By a circular telegram Shi Yu-san formally announces his retirement.
Yen Shi-shan and Feng Yu-hsiang (馮玉祥) confer at the Taiyuan Military Conference. The Conference resolves to support the Canton regime.
Eugene Chen leaves Tokyo.
Tai Chi-tao (戴季陶), President of the Examination Yuan, dismissed from his office.
China protest to Japan on military manoeuvres on the Tumen River (圖們江).
Relation between Wang Ching-wei and Chen Chi-tang severed. Wang leaves Canton for Hongkong.
News of the murder of Captain Nakamura released.
Japanese authorities protest to Chinese authorities in Manchuria on the murder of Captain Nakamura.
Japanese Patriotic organization at Tsingtao attacked by Chinese.
Wang Ching-wei returns to Canton after successful mediation by Sun Fo and Tang Shao-yi. Hsu Chung-chih (許崇智) appointed the Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Expedition against Nanking.
Chinese Government demands apology of the Japanese Government for anti-Chinese riots in Korea.
Tang Erh-ho (湯爾和) meets Japanese military authorities in Tokyo as the special envoy of Chang Hsueh-liang.
China requests the United States to intervene in the dispute with Mexico regarding the deportation of the Chinese.
Northern Expedition of Canton starts..
Japanese Consul-General Hayashi presents to Mukden authorities the Japanese demands on the Captain Nakamura case.
Colonel Doihara of the Mukden Special Service of the Kwantung Army arrives at Tokyo.
Tang Erh-ho, special envoy of Chang Hsueh-liang, returns to Peiping.
Major Shibayama, Military Advisor to Chang Hsueh-liang, arrives at Tokyo.
Minister Shigemitsu presents credentials to the Nanking Government.
China elected to the Council of the League of Nations.
Colonel Doihara leaves Tokyo for Mukden.
Commander Kuan Yu-heng (關玉衡), who was responsible for the murder of Captain Nakamura, brought to Mukden and detained in a military prison.
Clash between Chinese and Japanese troops, following the destruction of the S.M.R. line at Liutiaokou (柳條溝).
Japanese troops occupy various cities along the S.M.R. line.
China protests to Japan on the occupation of Mukden.
China sends a note to the League of Nations and also to the United States.
Second protest of China to Japan.
Provisional Municipal Office of Mukden opened, Colonel Doihara, Chief of the Japanese Special Military Service at Mukden, being appointed the Mayor.
Kirin occupied by Japanese troops.
Shih Chao-chi or Alfred Sze (施肇基) Chinese delegate to the League, appeals to the League under Article 11 of the Covenant.
Great Britain suspends Gold embargo.
Council meeting of the League held on Sino-Japanese dispute.
Telegram sent by the Chairman of the Council of the League of Nations (M. Lerroux) to Japan and China, asking to refrain from any action that might aggravate the situation.
Third protest sent by China to Japan.
United States sends a note to the League of Nations.
Identic note of the United States addressed to Japan and China.
China replies to the telegram of M. Lerroux, Chairman of the League Council.
Japan issues the first official statement on the Manchurian situation.
By a statement China officially refuses direct negotiation with Japan.
Japan replies to the telegram of the Chairman of the League Council dated September 22.
Japanese troops occupy Taonan.
Murder of six Japanese by Chinese mobs at Hongkong.
Liaoning Local Committee for Preservation of Peace and Order (遼寧地方維持委員會) formed at Mukden.
Japan and China reply to the United States note of Sept. 24.
Liaoning Provincial Government established at Chinchow (錦州) under the influence of the former Mukden authority.
C. T. Wang, Nanking Foreign Minister, severely wounded by student mobs.
Independence of Kirin, Heilungkiang and Jehol provinces declared.
Japanese Government orders Japanese officials in Manchuria to keep aloof of the independence movement.
China protests to Japan on the alleged support given for the independence movement.
Resolution of the League Council on the Manchurian situation adopted.
Japan replies to the protest of China under the date of Sept. 29.

Chang Chi (張繼), Chen Ming-shu (陳銘樞), Tsai Yuan-pei (蔡元培) delegates of the Nanking Government, meet at Canton the representatives of Canton government, namely Ku Ying-fen, Wang Ching-wei, and Wu Chao-shu. Compromise reached between the two governments..
Chang Hai-feng (張海鵬) of Taonan declares independence.
China asks the members of the League Council and the United States to send neutral observers to Manchuria.
Peace Conference (和平會議) at Canton opened with the attendance of both Canton and Nanking delegates.
Statement of the Kwantung Army issued.
American observers sent to Mukden.
Bombardment of Chinchow by Japanese Air Forces..
Japan issues a memorandum to China protesting anti-Japanese boycott and other activities.
U.S. note to the League of Nations.
Identic telegram sent by the Chairman of the League Council (M. Lerroux) to Japan and China.
U.S. memorandum to Japan on the Chinchow incident.
Japan replies to the telegram of the League Council's Chairman.
China replies to Japan's protest on boycott.
Council of the League of Nations holds its session on the Sino-Japanese dispute.
Business suspended at Harbin due to the severe fall of Harbin Tayang-piao.
Troops of Chang Hai-feng move northward to Tsitsihar.
Provincial Bank of the Three Eastern Provinces and the Frontier Bank reopened.
Mukden-Hailung (Chaoyangchen) Railway resumes operation.
While retreating to Tsitsihar, troops of the Heilungkiang Army burn down railway bridges across the Nonni River.
United States accepts the invitation of the League Council.
League Council decides to invite the U.S. observer.
Clash between the troops under Chang Hai-feng and those under Ma Chan-shan (馬占山).
Japan questions on the legality of inviting the U.S. observers to the Council meeting.
Identic notes reminding the obligation under the Kellog Pact addressed to Japan and China by thirteen signatory nations.
Japanese authorities in China issue a note presenting the cases of China's violation of treaties.
Chairman of the League Council (M. Briand) replies to Japan's inquiry on the question of the U.S. observer.
New Liaoning Provincial Government under the influence of the independence movement opened at Mukden.
Big student demonstration held at Nanking.
Chao Hsin-po (趙欣伯) appointed the Mayor of Mukden.
Fourth Conference of the Institute of Pacific Relations opened at Shanghai.
China replies to the governments invoking the Kellogg Pact.
Japan replies to the notes sent by the Kellogg Pact signatory nations.
Resolution submitted to the League Council, Japan dissenting.
Second statement of the Japanese Government.
China issues a statement on the League Council's resolution of Oct. 24.
Second Preliminary Conference for the peace negotiation between Nanking and Canton opened.
Japan asks Soviet authorities to stop concentrating troops near the Manchurian border.
Briand's (League council's chairman) note on Japan's statement of Oct. 26.
Karakhan's statement on the Manchurian dispute.
Chang Hsueh-liang arrives at Nanking to confer with Chiang Kaishek on the Manchurian situation.
China replies to Japan's statement of October. 26.
New North-Eastern Communications Committee formed at Mukden.
Kirin-Changchun Railway Bureau and the Kirin-Tunhwa Railway Bureau amalgamated.
C. T. Wang resigns from the post of Foreign Minister.
Japanese troops march northward from Taonan toward Tsitsihar to protect the reconstructing operations of the Nonni River bridges.
Clash between Japanese troops and Ma Chan-shan forces in Nonni River region.
United States Minister at Tokyo presents a memorandum on the North Manchurian situation.
Chairman of the League Council (M. Briand) sends a note on the seizure of the salt gabelle revenue at Yingkow to the Japanese representative to the League.
Statement on the North Manchurian situation issued by the Japanese Military authorities.
Japanese and Chinese delegates to the League report on the situation in the Nonni River district.
Chairman of the League Council announces his decision to reopen the Council meeting on Nov. 16.
Identic telegram sent by the Chairman of the League Council (M. Briand) to Japan and China.
Liaoning Local Committee for Preservation of Peace and Order proclaims to assume the duty of Provincial government.
Japan replies to the note of the Chairman of the League Council.
Riots occur in Tientsin.
Pu-yi (溥儀), ex-Emperor of China, secretly leaves Tientsin.
Liaoning Self-Government Guiding Office (遼寧自治指導部) formed under the leadership of Yu Chung-han (于沖漢).
Japan replies to the U.S. note of Oct. 5.
Quotation of silver recovers and reaches 21, 1/16.
Secretary Stimson sends instructions to General Dawes, the U.S. Minister at Paris on the coming League Council meeting.
Liaoning Local Committee for Preservation of Peace and Order proclaims its plan for financial reorganization and its principle in preparing new budget for 1931-32.
Kirin provincial government abolishes some taxes.
Captain Walters of the League of Nations leaves Shanghai for Tokyo.
China protests to Japan on sending troops to Heilungkiang Province.
Second identic note sent by the Chairman of the League Council (M. Briand) to Japan and China on the North Manchurian situation.
China replies to the telegram sent by the Chairman of the League Council on Nov. 11.
Japan protests to China on the Tientsin incident.
Fourth Kuomintang Congress opened in Nanking.
Japan replies to the telegram of the Chairman of the League Council of Nov. 11.
Japan's ultimatum presented to Ma Chan-shan.
China replies to Japan's protest on the Tientsin incident.
Soviet sends a statement on the situation in Heilungkiang Province to Japan.
Third Council meeting of the League of Nations on the Sino-Japanese dispute opened at Paris.
China protests to Japan on the Nonni River incident.
Vanguard of Japanese troops enter Tsitsihar.
Fourth National Congress of Party Delegates convened by Canton formally opened.
Japan replies to the Soviet statement of Nov. 14.
Second Soviet Statement sent to Japan.
Japanese Air Forces attack Hailun.
Liaoning Province renamed Fengtien Province.
Chinese and Japanese delegates consent in principle to the proposal made by Japan for sending a commission under the League to investigate the situation in Manchuria.
China lodges third protest on Japan's military action in North Manchuria.
Identic telegram sent by the Chairman of the League Council (M. Briand) to Japan and China on the situation in the Chinchow district.
Shih Chao-chi, Chinese delegate, asks the League Council to establish a neutral zone between present stations of the two forces.
China protests to Japan on Japanese military action extending westward to Chinchow.
Clash between Japanese and Chinese troops at Tientsin.
Westward movement of Japanese troops along the Peiping-Mukden Railway ordered to stop.
Alleged statement of Secretary Stimson causes obstruction in the American-Japanese relation.
Sun Fo and Eugene Chen of the Canton faction declare independence of Canton.
Japanese military authorities at Tokyo issue a statement on military activities of Japanese troops in Liaohsi district (Chinchow region).
China issues a statement on the situation in the Chinchow district
Japan declines the League Council's proposal to station neutral observers in the neutral zone of Chinchow.
Chiang Kai-shek sends a telegram to Wang Ching-wei at Shanghai inviting Canton Leaders to Nanking for First Plenary Session of the new Central Executive Committee of Kuomintang.
Statement issued by the Military authorities of Japan on the second Chinchow incident.
Student demonstrators occupy three railway stations at Peiping.
Neutral foreign observers in reports to League deny tales of Chinese activities in Chinchow region.
After negotiations with Japanese military authorities, Ma Chanshan decides his allegiance to the new authority in Manchuria.
Resolution on the Manchurian situation adopted by the League Council.
U.S. Statement endorses the Council's resolution.
Big student demonstration takes place at Nanking.
Sun Fo and other members of the Canton Peace Delegation arrive at Shanghai.
Wakatsuki Cabinet of Japan resigns.
Inukai Cabinet formed in Japan.
Gold embargo suspended in Japan.
Tsang Shih-yi (臧式毅), ex-Governor of Liaoning Province, sworn in as Chairman of the Fengtien Provincial Government.
Chiang Kai-shek formally resigns from all his posts in the Government.
Resignation of Chang Hsueh-liang as the Deputy Commander-in-Chief accepted. He was appointed the Pacification Commissioner for Peiping.
Chiang Kai-shek resigning, the Canton delegates arrive at Nanking.
Japanese War Ministry issues a statement on the necessity of sending troops to Chinchow.
Kwantung Army commences activity to suppress disorderly element in Liaohsi district.
Japanese military authorities issue a statement upon the urgency of adopting military action against bandits.
First Plenary Session of the new Central Executive Committee and the Supervisory Committee of the Kuomintang.
Japanese Diet opened.
United States sends a note to Japan on the situation in the Chinchow region.
Japan issues a statement on the anti-bandit compaign in the Chinchow district.
Japan replies to the U.S. note of Dec. 24.
New Nanking National Government formed under the Chairmanship of Lin Sen (林森).
Chang Hsueh-liang orders his troops to retreat from Chinchow to the west of Shanhaikwan.
Yoshizawa, Japanese Minister to France, meets Litvinoff at Moscow on his way back to Tokyo.
Japanese troops occupy Kuopantzu (濤帮子) on Peking-Mukden line.
Vanguard of Japanese troops enter Chinchow.
Chang Ching-hui, new Governor of Heilungkiang Province, declares the independence of Heilungkiang Province at Harbin.
Identic note of the U.S. sent to Japan and China.
Eastern section of the Peiping-Mukden Railway renamed the Fengshan (Fengtien-Shanhaikwan) Railway.
Abusive article on the Japanese Imperial Household appears in the "Minkuo Jih-pao' (民國日報), newspaper published at Shanghai.
Anti-Kirin troops start opposition against new regime under Hsi Hsia (熙洽).
China replies to the U.S. note of Jan. 8.
Protocol signed between China and Japan in Dec. 1905 respecting 'parallel railway lines' in Manchuria made public by the Japanese Foreign Ministry.
Japan replies to the U.S. note of Jan. 8.
Japanese priests severely wounded (one of whom died 5 days later) by Chinese mobs at Shanghai.
Owing to financial difficulties, the Nanking Government decides to take severe retrenchment measures.
Japanese Consul-General Murai at Shanghai presents Japanese demands to Mayor Wu of Greater Shanghai.
Clash between Chinese and Japanese demonstrators at Shanghai.
Japanese Diet dissolved.
Commission of Enquiry into the Sino-Japanese Dispute of the League of Nations organized with Lord Lytton as the Chairman.
66th League Council Meeting opened under the chairmanship of M. Boncour.
Mayor Wu replies to Japan, agreeing to Japanese demands.
Clash between Japanese Marines and the 19th Route Army at Shanghai.
China appeals to the League of Nations under Article 15 of the League Covenant.
Japan issues a statement on the Shanghai situation.
Anti-Kirin faction under Ting Chao (丁超) occupies Harbin.
Mayor Wu protests to the Shanghai Municipal Council on Japan's use of the International Settlement for military purposes.
China sends an identic note to the signatories of the Nine-Power Treaty.
Anglo-American protest against Japan's use of the Shanghai International Settlement.
Wang Ching-wei appointed the Chief of the Executive Yuan, Nanking Government.
United States, Great Britain, and France propose a conciliating plan for settling the Shanghai incident.
Disarmament Conference opened at Geneva.
Enquiry Commission of the League of Nations leaves Paris for Tokyo.
China accepts the Four-powers' proposal.
Japan replies to the Four-powers' proposal.
Vanguard of Japanese troops enter Harbin.
Operation of the southern line of the C.E.R. resumed.
Japan issues a statement on the Shanghai situation and the despatch of Military Forces.
Japanese Government decides to send Y. Matsuoka to Shanghai on special mission.
First Report of the League Shanghai Committee (dated Feb. 6.) released.
Inouye, Finance Minister of the former Japanese Cabinet, assassinated.
China requests to convene extraordinary assembly of the League of Nations.
Japanese Army lands at Shanghai.
Shanghai Municipal Council issues a statement on the relation of the International Settlement with the Powers.
Second report of the League Shanghai Committee (dated Feb. 12) released.
China protests to Great Britain and the United States.
Twelve members of the League Council appeal to Japan.
Preparatory Conference for the establishment of a New State in Manchuria held, Tsang Shi-yi, Chang Ching-hui, Hsi Hsia, Ma Chan-shan and Chao Hsin-po present.
Declaration of independence of the Four North-Eastern Provinces issued by the Administrative Committee of the North-Eastern Provinces (東北行政委員會).
Japanese Army presents ultimatum to the Chinese Army at Shanghai.
League Council decides to convene Extraordinary Assembly.
Third report of the League Shanghai Committee submitted.
Attack by Japanese troops started at Shanghai.
China replies to Japan's ultimatum.
General election takes place in Japan.
China issues a statement on the 'independence movement' in Manchuria.
Japan replies to the League Council's appeal of Feb. 16.
China protests to Japan on the recent political development in Manchuria.
Secretary Stimson sends a letter to Senator Borah on the Nine-Power Treaty.
North-Eastern Administrative Committee decides on general principles of the new administration in Manchuria.
Foreign Minister Yoshizawa of Japan proposes a round table conference in Shanghai.
Japan explains to China regarding the latter's protests made on Feb. 24.
Chairman of the League Council (M. Boncour) proposes armistice at Shanghai.
League's Enquiry Commission arrives at Tokyo.
Establishment of Manchoukuo proclaimed.
General Shirakawa appointed the Commander-in-Chief of the Shanghai Expedition Army of Japan..
China protests on Japan's activities regarding establishing the New State in Manchuria.
Last stage of the military action at Shanghai.
Cessation of hostilities ordered by Japanese Commander-in-Chief.
Resolution on the Shanghai situation adopted at the special session of the League Assembly.
Pu-yi accepts the invitation to become the Chief Executive of Manchoukuo.
Baron Dan assassinated at Tokyo.
Loyang (洛陽) Conference decides to form the Anti-Japanese Military Committee (抗日軍事委員會), and to appoint Chiang Kai-shek the Chairman.
China accepts the proposal of the League Council's Chairman made on Feb. 29.
Fourth Report of the League Shanghai Committee (dated March 4) released.
Pu-yi, the new Chief Executive of Manchoukuo, arrives at Changchun.
Chiang Kai-shek again appointed the Commander-in-Chief of National Forces.
Japan sends a note on the negotiation for the cessation of hostilities.
State ceremony of the establishment of Manchoukuo held in the presence of the Chief Executive at Changchun.
China replies to Japan's note of March 8.
Resolution on the Shanghai situation adopted at the special session of the League Assembly, Japan abstaining from voting.
China calls the new Manchurian government a 'Rebel Organization'.
United States endorses the League Assembly's resolution.
Communication of the Foreign Minister of Manchoukuo on the establishment of a New State despatched to the Powers.
Manchoukuo opens negotiations to obtain a loan of ¥20,000,000 from Japan.
League Commission of Enquiry arrives at Shanghai.
Changchun, the capital of Manchoukuo, renamed Hsinching (新京).
Special Session of the Japanese Diet.
Minister Hirota of Japan to Moscow warns on alleged concentration of Soviet troops near the Korean border.
Japan replies to the protest of China dated March 1.
Japan replies to Manchoukuo's note of March 12.
U.S. Minister Forbes at Tokyo leaves Japan for home.
Second protest of China to Japan on her responsibility towards the new development in Manchuria.
Manchoukuo's statement regarding Customs tariff issued.
Manchoukuo declares independence of the salt administration in the territory under her authority.
New Province of Khingan (or Hsingan) inaugurated.
Japan replies to the Chinese protest of March 24.
Manchoukuo decides to seize the Postal Administration in Manchuria.
China protests to Japan on the question of the salt gabelle of Manchuria.
Mitsui and Mitsubishi financial concerns of Japan propose to contribute ¥20,000,000 for the economic development of Manchoukuo.
Part of the Japanese Army in Korea despatched to Chientao to attack the anti-Kirin troops in Kirin Province.
Ma Chan-shan revolts against Manchoukuo and disappears from Tsitsihar.
League Commission of Enquiry arrives at Hankow.
Vice-President Eguchi of the S.M.R. Co. resigns.
Anti-Kirin troops under Wang Te-lin (王錫林) annihilated.
Secretary Stimson leaves New York for Geneva.
By a telegram to the Nanking authorities, the Foreign Minister of Manchoukuo refuses the entrance of Ku Wei-chun (顧維均) or Wellington Koo, Chinese Assessor to the League Commission, into Manchoukuo.
League Commission of Enquiry arrives at Peiping.
Japanese military train derailed near Harbin, resulting in many casualties.
Japan declares her intention of protecting Ku Wei-chun while he remains within the sphere where Japanese authority prevails.
Fengtien Provincial Office issues an order to restrict the entrance of foreigners and Chinese coolies.
League Commission of Enquiry arrives at Dairen.
Japanese syndicate banks and insurance companies decide to finance ₩40,000,000 to the S.M.R. Co.
League Commission of Enquiry formally visits the Japanese Consulate-General at Mukden.
League Commission of Enquiry makes the first call on General Honjo of the Kwantung Army.
Lord Lytton sends a telegram to the Foreign Minister of Manchoukuo.
Foreign Minister of Manchoukuo replies to Lord Lytton's telegram.
Attempt on the lives of Japanese high officials made at Shanghai by a Korean. General Shirakawa, Minister Shigemitsu, Lieutenant-General Uyeda and others wounded.
League Commission of Enquiry presents its Preliminary Report to the League.
League Commission of Enquiry leaves Mukden for Changchun.
Kuo Tai-chi (郭泰祺), the Chinese Chief delegate to the Shanghai Peace Conference, attacked and wounded by students.
Preliminary Report of the League Enquiry Commission released.
Shanghai Peace Agreement signed.
League Enquiry Commission meets the Chief Executive of Manchoukuo.
Evacuation of Japanese troops at Shanghai commenced.
League Commission of Enquiry leaves Changchun for Harbin.
Japanese troops at Shanghai ordered to evacuate completely.
League Commission of Enquiry asks to meet Ma Chan-shan; the demand is declined by the Manchoukuo authorities..
Prime Minister Inukai of Japan assassinated at Tokyo.
Seiyukai (Inukai) Cabinet of Japan resigns.
League Commission of Enquiry leaves Harbin for Mukden.
Kuo Tai-chi appointed the Foreign Minister of the Nanking Government.
Saito Cabinet formed in Japan.
League Commission of Enquiry returns to Dairen.
League Commission of Enquiry leaves Dairen for Peiping via Mukden.
Withdrawal of Japanese troops at Shanghai completed.
Special Session of the Japanese Diet.
Japanese troops occupy Hailun.
League Commission of Enquiry leaves Manchuria.
Manchoukuo announces the revolt of Ma Chan-shan.
Finance Ministry of Manchoukuo issues regulations regarding the Central Bank and currencies.
Nanking Government issues a statement attacking Japan's intention to recognize Manchoukuo.
Manchoukuo Finance Ministry sends a statement to the Nanking Government on the question of the Dairen Customs House.
Sung Tzu-wen or T. V. Soon (宋子文), the Nanking Minister of Finance issues a statement on the question of the Dairen Customs House.
Fukumoto, Commissioner of the Dairen Customs House, dismissed by the Inspector-General of the Chinese Maritime Customs.
China protests to Japan on Manchoukuo's seizure of the Dairen Customs House.
Manchoukuo issues a statement on the Customs Tariff autonomy.
Japan protests to China on the dismissal of Commissioner Fukumoto of the Dairen Customs House.
Customs Houses at Yingkow and Antung taken over by Manchoukuo.
Central Bank of Manchoukuo (Central Bank of Manchou) opened.
League Commission of Enquiry arrives at Tokyo for the second visit.
Count Uchida, ex-President of the S.M.R. Co., appointed the Foreign Minister of Japan.
Harbin Customs House seized by Manchoukuo.
League Commission of Enquiry meets General Araki, Minister of War of Japan.
Communications Department of Manchoukuo demands the complete surrender of the postal administration of the high foreign officials of the postal service.
First interview between Count Uchida and the League Commission of Enquiry at Tokyo.
Second interview between Count Uchida and the League Commission of Enquiry at Tokyo.
Lord Lytton leaves Tokyo for China.
Dispute between the S.M.R. Co., and the Mine Owners' Association of Japan on the import of Fushun coal settled.
Ishimoto, interpreter of the Kwantung Army, arrested near Chaoyang by the Volunteer Army under Chang Hsueh-liang.
League Commission of Enquiry arrives at Peiping.
National Government decides to close Manchurian Customs Houses.
Nanking Government agrees to the appointment of Ariyoshi as the Minister to China.
Nanking Government announces closing of the postal adminstration in Manchuria since July 2.
Hsiehhohui 協和會) or Kyowakai inaugurated.
Count Hayashi appointed the President of the S.M.R. Co.
Unification and consolidation of Japanese authorities in Manchuria decided.
Ariyoshi formally appointed the Japanese Minister to China.
Ma Chan-shan reported to have died.
Sung Tsu-wen, Finance Minister of Nanking, declares suspension of payment of the Boxer Indemnity to Japan.
New import tariff of China announced.
Flood reported to threaten the City of Harbin.
Chang Hsueh-liang tenders his resignation.
General Muto appointed the Commander-in-Chief of the Kwantung Army and Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary.
Flood reported in North Manchuria.
Soviet-Japanese Fishery Agreement signed.

By the resignation of Chang Hsueh-liang, the Peiping Pacification Commissioner's Office abolished; Chiang Kai-shek to be the Chief of the newly established Peiping Branch of the Central Military Committee.
Nanking Foreign Office issues a statement on the appointment of General Muto.
Chiang Kai-shek, Wang Ching-wei and Lin Sen meet at Lushan (盧山).
Third Special Session of the Japanese Diet opened.
Count Uchida, Japanese Foreign Minister, announces his policy in respect to the recognition of Manchoukuo.
National Congress for abolishing civil war held at Shanghai.
Nanking Foreign Minister, Lo Wen-kan (羅文幹), issues a statement on Count Uchida's speech delivered at the Japanese Diet on August 25.
Manchoukuo protests to the Nanking Government and Chang Hsueh-liang on the instigation of the Volunteer Army in Jehol Province.
Chang Tsung-chang (張宗昌) assassinated at the Tsinan railway station.
Ariyoshi, new Japanese Minister to China, arrives at Shanghai.
League Commission of Enquiry leaves Peiping.
Special Session of the Japanese Diet closed.
Manchoukuo-Japan Protocol signed.
China protests on the recognition of Manchoukuo by Japan.
New Dairen Customs House of Manchoukuo established.
China sends a note to the League of Nations.
China sends an identic note on her attitude towards new Manchoukuo-Japan Protocol to the signatories of the Nine-Power Treaty.
68th Council Meeting of the League of Nations opened.
13th Assembly meeting of the League of Nations opened.
Pao Kuan-cheng (鮑觀登), First Envoy of Manchoukuo to Japan, arrives at Tokyo.
Report of the Commission of Enquiry of the League of Nations delivered to Japan and China.
Report of the Commission of Enquiry of the League of Nations released.
